A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable 23-page versions of the same study. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison despite the revised title and substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark experiments with seven LLMs, a 300-rationale human evaluation, and supplementary context-length and rationale-similarity analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and additionally reports quantitative measurements of rationale length.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same eight-example prompting construction, answer-generation procedures and task instructions. Implicit examples still contain questions, incorrect answers and correct answers without corrective rationales. The added verification statement does not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate GSM8K, ASDiv, open-ended AQuA and PRM800K on the same labelling, editing and solving tasks. The GSM8K human evaluation and three-dataset preliminary CoT-2 experiment are also retained.

E2.justification: CoT and explicit prompting remain the main comparators, with CoT+ and CoT-2 as context controls. CoT-2 already appears in v1 Appendix A; its inclusion in v2 Section 5.1 is not a new baseline.

E3.justification: V2 adds mean character length as a rationale-analysis metric and revises Command R+'s reported size from 100B to 104B in Section 4.1. The API identifiers, benchmark settings and preliminary CoT-2 labelling protocol remain unchanged; no model replacement or rerun is established.

E4.justification: V2 Section 5.2 adds a quantitative comparison of generated and exemplar rationale lengths to investigate verbosity and possible overfitting. The context controls, human evaluation, bigram-similarity analysis and representative rationale case study already existed in v1.

E5.justification: Five-run averaging and the table reporting conventions are retained. V2 additionally displays error bars in the new aggregate CoT+ comparison, Figure 4, without explaining what they represent. No increased run count or new significance test is reported.

E6.justification: V2 newly reports mean lengths of 373 characters for explicit rationales, 237 for implicit rationales and 423 for exemplars. Between v1 Table 4 and v2 Table 6, PRM800K CoT-2/implicit answer-labelling values change from 34.4/35.5 to 69.9/70.7, with step-labelling values changing in reverse. The main benchmark, CoT+, human-rating and similarity tables otherwise retain their results.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(3) and the formal construction of prompts and task combinations are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations are added or removed.

C1.justification: The main performance claims remain. However, v2 strengthens the tentative overfitting explanation into an explicit contribution and an abstract/conclusion claim that corrective rationales limit learning by over-constraining models. This replaces human-rated rationale quality as the third listed contribution, while retaining that finding.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new length measurements as further confirmation of overfitting, beyond v1's cautious similarity-based hypothesis. It also explicitly acknowledges that applicability outside mathematical reasoning remains untested, while retaining the limitation concerning fine-tuning.

D1.justification: Section 3.3 newly states that corrective rationales are verified for correctness. V2 replaces the repository link for all datasets' exemplars with an unspecified OpenReview attachment reference, and drops the explicit statement identifying the similarity-analysis corpus as the human-evaluation corpus. Actual external resource availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 adds Zhang et al. (2024), In-context principle learning from mistakes, and removes four psychology references alongside the human-learning analogy. It also newly positions the context-length investigation as missing from prior literature. The broader LLM-related research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and much of the introduction are rewritten. Discussion becomes Analysis, integrating CoT-2 and rationale similarity into the main narrative. Detailed human-evaluation findings and representative rationales move to appendices, which are substantially reordered.

P2.justification: V2 adds the CoT+ summary Figure 4 and redraws/compresses Figure 2. Visual evidence is substantially redistributed: main CoT+ Table 2 becomes appendix Table 5, appendix similarity Table 6 becomes main Table 3, and the human-rating chart and rationale boxes move to appendices.

improvement.justification: V2 improves the organization of the analyses and adds rationale-length evidence and an explicit domain limitation. However, access information becomes less actionable, and the overfitting explanation is strengthened without a new test isolating that mechanism. With the central experiments unchanged, these benefits and drawbacks do not establish a reliable net direction in overall quality.
